decision: User explicitly chose single_core_two_views. Historical independent-parser differences are evidence only, NOT acceptance blockers for this route.
historicalCommand: npm run diagnostic:historical-cross-core (expected current exit 1; original strict failures preserved)
implemented: Actual singleton boxed alacritty Term + persistent Processor, Native/Webview attachments, full snapshot then coalesced row changes with base revision, output sequence, epoch, first-frame ACK, timed commit, bounded input freeze queue. No bytes sent to either view, no query replay, no core detach/recreation.

productionSeam.lifetime: TerminalEngine remains session-owned in EngineRegistry. start(SharedOutput) runs once and owns output receiver; view changes MUST NOT call engine.close/remove/start or resume session.poll.
productionSeam.sink: Current set_sink replaces a single sink and marks full_pending. Keep a stable session-owned fanout sink attached once. Fanout manages two view epochs, last acknowledged baseline, max one in-flight frame per view and explicit request_full on attach/gap. Do NOT set_sink(None) for a view switch while the old view must remain visible.
productionSeam.snapshot: snapshot_frame() currently increments engine seq and can reset damage while encoding. Capture snapshot + canonical output_seq/revision under the same engine inner lock or encode once/fanout; do not race an out-of-band full with emit. Prototype uses safe serialized &mut access but production locking is not implemented here.
productionSeam.wire: frame::FrameHeader seq is wrapping u32, no output_seq/epoch/base revision. Preserve current binary field; put session id, attachment epoch, u64 canonical revision/output_seq and base revision into an outer envelope or negotiated protocol v2. Never compare wrapping seq as plain monotonic integer; use epoch + u64 revision or serial-number arithmetic with bounded outstanding frames.
productionSeam.damage: Encode once from canonical Term damage, not once per view resetting global damage. A lagging attachment requests full instead of growing byte/revision logs. Prototype Frame carries full snapshot plus changed_rows/base metadata as executable protocol proof; it is NOT a production compact wire encoder.
productionSeam.ack: Renderer applied ACK must identify session+view epoch+revision. GPU/DOM first_frame ACK must follow actual frame presentation of same revision; this prototype only calls a modeled first_frame method. Old view remains until atomic commit succeeds at current revision.
productionSeam.input: Catchup does not freeze input. begin_commit is allowed only after target parsed/applied+presented current revision; freeze user input briefly into total 128-byte queue, apply backpressure on overflow. Keep output ingress/protocol responses flowing; output changing tail invalidates readiness. Timeout/cancel drains accepted input to unchanged session and keeps old view.
productionSeam.authority: Only canonical Processor emits PTY/clipboard/title side effects. Views receive state, never terminal escape byte stream and never generate device-query responses. Production response transport must remain independently backpressured; prototype listener is a drainable test collection, not a globally bounded PTY outbox.
productionSeam.history: Canonical Term owns full configured scrollback and alt/normal state. Prototype full snapshots include history text, cells, palette, cursor/mode metadata; production viewport/history paging should reference same core revision, never export plain text to reconstruct parser state.

limits: No native/Webview renderer implemented in this crate
No actual GPU or DOM presentation ACK
No production integration or version edits
Snapshot cells use Debug serialization in the spike, not stable wire ABI
Canonical history capped at 5000 lines; terminal protocol end states beyond fixtures not universal ANSI proof
